rationales.LC: The attack is a direct JSON-RPC tools/call with a URL field, not a natural-language path to a privileged decision; no attacker language influences agent behaviour.
rationales.CP: ToolBot is a stateless MCP tool server; the request and response leave no carryover context or memory, and the lab documents memory only for MemoryBot.
rationales.AP: The attacker uses ToolBot as a proxy to reach other DVAA agents on loopback ports, crossing a component boundary from the tool server into internal agent services.
rationales.RH: No evaluator, verifier, or reward channel exists on this path; ToolBot is a scripted tool server with no proxy objective, and no reward-hacking episode is possible or observed.
rationales.ES: Tools are a fixed advertised list, but fetch_url's URL argument has no validation, leaving a material argument-schema gap that permits SSRF to internal targets.

LC: Entry point: A JSON-RPC tools/call request to ToolBot (port 7010) that names fetch_url. No authentication.
CP: Other chat agents answer only the latest user turn. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1841-1848)
MemoryBot keeps up to 50 flagged messages in one in-process list shared by every caller. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:159-160)
AP: Attacker calls fetch_url with url http://localhost:7003/info.
The server returns the internal agent's response body to the attacker.
ToolBot fetch_url can make a live request to another DVAA agent port. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2079-2096)
RH: No shell runs. The command is logged and a few commands (ls, cat, env, find) are emulated against sandbox files. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1906-1914)
ToolBot role: MCP tool server: read_file, write_file, execute, fetch_url against a temporary sandbox directory. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:154-197)
ES: The handler has no URL validation. It makes a live request when the target is a DVAA agent port on loopback.
Makes a live request only to DVAA agent ports on loopback. Any other URL is logged and not fetched. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:2066-2106)
MCP agents expose their tools to any caller with no authentication. (damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1915-1926)

score.automatable_rationale: The documented PoC is a single curl command against an unauthenticated network port, with an automated test in the repo (test/mcp-tool-containment.test.js:72-87).
score.technical_impact_rationale: The SSRF discloses internal service response bodies (and in cloud deployments could reach metadata endpoints) but does not by itself compromise or modify the internal services.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default configuration no model is called; ToolBot is a scripted MCP tool server whose handlers execute fixed code, so no model directs goals or selects actions.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models ToolBot as a tool server with deterministic handlers (read_file, write_file, execute, fetch_url); even in LLM mode no tools are passed to the model, so the model never directs tool invocation.
